<ol>
<li>One number: at the base inputs, a 24-month wait costs the developer $171.1M in present value, and other customers $14.7M.</li>
<li>Scenarios, with no chance attached: the developer's cost is $88.8M, $171.1M and $247.3M for waits of 12, 24 and 36 months.</li>
<li>One at a time: the margin swings the developer's cost most, from $137.8M to $204.4M; capital and the discount rate swing it by $28.5M and $28.0M.</li>
<li>Stacked corners: every input at its low-cost end gives $111.8M; at its high-cost end, $234.7M.</li>
<li>Sampling 10 runs with seed 7: plain random leaves 4 of 10 margin slices and 3 of 10 discount-rate slices empty; a Latin hypercube leaves none.</li>
<li>1,000 Latin hypercube runs: median $170.3M; 80% of runs from $140.9M to $200.1M; the runs span $120.0M to $230.2M.</li>
<li>Near a corner (margin, capital and discount rate all in the same outer tenth of their ranges): 2 runs; a chance of 0.1³ per corner predicts 2.</li>
<li>Monte Carlo error over 20 seeds: P90 $200.1M ± $1.3M (two standard errors) with 1,000 runs, ± $4.7M with 100.</li>
<li>A chance under these inputs: above $200M, 0.0% of runs at 12 months, 10.1% at 24 and 92.9% at 36.</li>
<li>Spearman's rank correlation with the developer's cost: margin 0.86 (rank 1); then capital 0.38 and discount rate 0.31 (tied, rank 2–3); with other customers' cost: upgrades 0.81 (rank 1); then never arrives 0.54 (rank 2).</li>
<li>Narrow the margin's range to ± $5,000: capital 0.64 and discount rate 0.59 (tied, rank 1–2), and the margin (0.47) ranks 3.</li>
</ol>

<div class="lx-datanote"><svg class="lx-ic" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.8" aria-hidden="true"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="8.5"/><path d="M12 11v5M12 8v.2"/></svg><ul>
<li><b>Toy:</b> the waiting load of case file <a href="cf7-cost-of-waiting.html">CF7</a>, 100 MW: illustrative round numbers in one price level (no inflation). Other customers pay the utility's costs (no large-load tariff); no bridge power.</li>
<li><b>Ranges:</b> invented around CF7's values, each uniform and drawn independently; the wait is a scenario of 12, 24 or 36 months.</li>
<li><b>Accounts:</b> present values, each run at its own discount rate, month by month; the two accounts are never added.</li>
<li><b>Sampling:</b> Latin hypercube, seed 7, generator mulberry32; percentiles by linear interpolation, as in <a href="k05-probability-statistics.html">K5</a>; Monte Carlo error from 20 repeats with seeds 1 to 20.</li>
</ul></div>
<p class="lx-hint" style="margin-top:.6rem">About 35 guided minutes in ten steps. Every run is computed in your browser; nothing is sent anywhere.</p>

::: {#explain .lx-sec}
::: {.lx-sec-h}
## What you just did, as diagrams
:::

```{=html}
<div id="m7-explain" class="lx-xgrid">
<div class="lx-fallback">
<dl class="lx-ideas">
<dt>Scenario</dt><dd>A what-if set of inputs; here the wait, 12, 24 or 36 months, each given no probability.</dd>
<dt>One at a time</dt><dd>Swing one input across its range, the others fixed: a tornado chart; it gives no chances.</dd>
<dt>Distribution</dt><dd>How likely each value of an input is; uniform here, every value in its range equally likely.</dd>
<dt>Latin hypercube</dt><dd>Cuts every range into N equal slices and draws exactly once in each, for all inputs at once.</dd>
<dt>Monte Carlo error</dt><dd>How far an estimate moves with another seed: report it with the run count.</dd>
<dt>Rank correlation</dt><dd>Spearman's ρ ranks inputs by influence within the assumed ranges, not in the world.</dd>
</dl>
</div>
</div>
```

```{=html}
<div class="lx-deepers">
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper · Modeler</span>The formulas: the toy, the Latin hypercube, ρ and the Monte Carlo error</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
```

- **The toy.** With $i = (1+r)^{1/12} - 1$ and $A = \frac{1 - (1+i)^{-\tau}}{i}$, the developer's cost is $D = (m P + K i)\,A$ and other customers' is $R = U i A + \min(0.5,\, h\tau)\, U (1+i)^{-\tau}$.
- **Symbols.** $m$ margin (\$ per MW a month), $P$ = 100 MW, $K$ idle capital (\$), $r$ yearly discount rate, $U$ upgrade cost (\$), $\tau$ the wait (months).
- **The never-arrives chance.** $h$ is in percentage points added a month, not compounded: $h\tau$ = 24 × 0.5 points = 12%, capped at 50%.
- **Latin hypercube.** Run $a$'s draw of input $j$ is $u_{a,j} = (\pi_j(a) + \xi_{a,j})/N$, with $\pi_j$ a random ordering of $0, \dots, N-1$ and $\xi$ uniform on $[0, 1)$; the value is $\text{lo} + u\,(\text{hi} - \text{lo})$.
- **Spearman's ρ.** The correlation of the ranks; with no ties, $\rho = 1 - \frac{6 \sum_a d_a^2}{N (N^2 - 1)}$, where $d_a$ is run $a$'s rank of the input minus its rank of the cost.
- **Monte Carlo error.** The standard error of an estimate is the standard deviation of that estimate over 20 repeats with other seeds; 20 repeats make the error itself rough, about ± 16%.
- **What the hypercube buys.** Over 20 seeds, the mean cost of 1,000 runs scatters by \$0.03M with a Latin hypercube and \$0.80M with plain random draws (one standard error); the P90, by \$0.65M and \$0.80M.
- **A share's error.** For plain random draws, K5's $\sqrt{p(1-p)/N}$ gives 0.95 points for the 10.1% above \$200M; the Latin hypercube repeats scatter by 0.52 points.
- **Near a corner.** With continuous inputs, an exact corner has zero chance. Near one (the margin, capital and discount rate all in the same outer tenth of their ranges) has 0.1³ = 0.1% per corner, so 1,000 runs expect 2; seed 7 has 2, both at the high-cost end.

```{=html}
</div>
</details>
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper · Modeler</span>What a rank correlation misses, and what comes next</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
```

- **Monotone effects only.** ρ reads how consistently the cost rises or falls with an input. An input that matters only through another (an interaction) or pushes the cost up and then down can show ρ near 0.
- **Variance shares.** Sobol indices split the variance of the cost among the inputs and their interactions; with $k$ inputs they need about $N(k+2)$ runs. The lab estimates them for this toy.
- **Inputs that move together.** Draw them with a stated rank correlation (Iman and Conover's method; the lab's practice task 3 uses a simplified two-input version), or sample whole records from data, as [K5](k05-probability-statistics.html) suggests.
- **Slow models.** When 1,000 runs take too long, a fast stand-in fitted to a few runs does the sampling ([M9](m09-surrogates-uq.qmd)); deciding before the uncertainty resolves is [M8](m08-stochastic-robust.qmd).

```{=html}
</div>
</details>
</div>
```
:::

## Check yourself, then try it
:::

```{=html}
<div class="lx-myths" data-quiz="m7-myth">
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="p90" data-answer="myth">
<p class="lx-qtext">Myth or fact? “A P90 of $200.1M means a 10% chance that the real wait costs more.”</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Myth. 10% of runs cost more, under the assumed ranges, uniform shapes and independent inputs. Change any of those and the P90 moves.</p></details>
</div>
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="runs" data-answer="myth">
<p class="lx-qtext">Myth or fact? “With 1,000 runs, a Monte Carlo answer is exact.”</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Myth. Over 20 seeds, the P90 of 1,000 runs scatters by ± $1.3M (2 standard errors). More runs shrink that; no run count fixes a wrong range.</p></details>
</div>
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="rank" data-answer="myth">
<p class="lx-qtext">Myth or fact? “The input with the largest rank correlation matters most in the real world.”</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Myth. ρ ranks inputs within the ranges you assumed: narrow the margin's to ± $5,000 and it drops from first to third.</p></details>
</div>
</div>

<div class="lx-quiz" data-quiz="m7">
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="share" data-answer="a">
<p class="lx-qtext">50 of 1,000 random runs exceed a budget. The share, with its standard error from K5's formula?</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="a">5.0% ± 0.7 points</li><li data-value="b">5.0% ± 5.0 points</li><li data-value="c">50% ± 1.6 points</li><li data-value="d">5.0%, exactly</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>5.0% ± 0.7 points: √(0.05 × 0.95 ÷ 1,000) = 0.0069, about 0.7 percentage points.</p></details>
</div>
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="report" data-answer="c">
<p class="lx-qtext">A report says only “P90 cost: $200M”. What should it add first?</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="a">More decimal places</li><li data-value="b">The cost at the base inputs</li><li data-value="c">Ranges and shapes, run count, seed and scatter</li><li data-value="d">The name of the computer it ran on</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>The inputs, the run count, the seed and the scatter: without them nobody can judge or repeat the P90.</p></details>
</div>
</div>
<div class="lx-card lx-case-try">
<p class="lx-eyebrow">Try it yourself with open code</p>
<p class="lx-hint">Optional, about 30 minutes; needs Python 3.10 or later (<a href="b02-python-data.html">lesson B2</a>).</p>
<ul>
<li>Clone and install the repository (its README's quick start), then write the illustrative files: <code>code-delay example my_scenario.json --grid grid.json --ranges ranges.json</code>.</li>
<li>Run <code>code-delay lhs my_scenario.json ranges.json --samples 500 --seed 1 --out-dir outputs/lhs</code>; open <code>rank_correlations.csv</code>.</li>
<li>Rerun with <code>--seed 2</code>. Do any two inputs swap places? Then treat them as tied, as step 9 does.</li>
</ul>

</div>
```
